instruction.text: Read the conversation between Leah and her mum and fill in the gaps with the correct words.

atoms.b: Mum, we talked about the internet in school today.
atoms.sound: ssml: <prosody pitch = '-1st'> Mum, we talked about the internet in school today.</prosody>

atoms.b: How interesting! Tell me more about it.
Did you know that the internet is a big ((++network router)) of lots of digital devices?
atoms.sound: ssml: <prosody pitch = '-1st'> Did you know that the internet is a big network of lots of digital devices?</prosody>

atoms.b: Yes. All the computers in the world with internet access can ((++connect sell)) to each other.
What else did you talk about?
atoms.sound: What else did you talk about?

atoms.b: We talked about how you get on the internet. You just open a ((++web_browser shop)) and type in an internet address.
atoms.sound: ssml: <prosody pitch = '-1st'> We talked about how you get on the internet. You just open a web browser and type in an internet address.</prosody>

atoms.b: Or another option is to download an ((++app connection)). That’s a program for smartphones where you can play games, chat with friends or learn things.
atoms.sound: ssml: <prosody pitch = '-1st'> Or another option is to download an app. That’s a program for smartphones where you can play games, chat with friends or learn things.</prosody>

atoms.b: Did you know that you can also download ((++pictures the_internet)) and documents from your browser?
That’s right. There was also another word that sounds really similar. Hmm...
atoms.sound: ssml: <prosody pitch = '-1st'> That’s right. There was also another word that sounds really similar. mmm...</prosody>

atoms.b: Yes, exactly! Uploading is the ((++opposite same)) of downloading: you load something onto the internet.
atoms.sound: ssml: <prosody pitch = '-1st'> Yes, exactly! Uploading is the opposite of downloading: you load something onto the internet. </prosody>

atoms.b: What surprised me the most was that all ((++data mail)) gets saved on the internet.
atoms.sound: ssml: <prosody pitch = '-1st'> What surprised me the most was that all data gets saved on the internet.</prosody>

atoms.b: What exactly were you surprised about?
That everything on the internet is saved somewhere, whether that’s ((++websites animals)), videos, pictures, ((++emails shoes)), messages or personal data.
atoms.sound: ssml: <prosody pitch = '-1st'> That everything on the internet is saved somewhere, whether that’s websites, videos, pictures, emails, messages or personal data. </prosody>

atoms.b: Not just anywhere, but on something called a ((++server phone)). That’s a lot of connected computers that save data. You can access these at any time.
